GO on io-imap; pin =0.6.0 (default-features=false + 'client'). All four open questions answered by source inspection; decision written to docs/decisions/0001-imap-library.md. (1) API churn: 0.5->0.6 changes only 3 files -- watch.rs, client.rs's watch_mailbox and lib.rs docs; everything we use is byte-identical, so adopt 0.6. Real risk is release velocity (6 minors in 11 weeks), mitigated by the existing MailBackend-only invariant. (2) QRESYNC/CONDSTORE ARE reachable: SelectParameter::{CondStore,QResync{..}}, FetchModifier::{ChangedSince,Vanished}, and ImapMailboxSelectData decodes highest_mod_seq + vanished_earlier + changed. E5's incremental sync design stands unchanged. Gaps: no UNCHANGEDSINCE on STORE, FETCH discards VANISHED (use SELECT QRESYNC instead), and watch::ImapMailboxWatch is unusable (whole-mailbox in-memory shadow). (3) Post-auth CAPABILITY re-read: yes via ImapSessionOpen/ImapClientStd::connect, which force ensure_capabilities=true; footgun is that the per-coroutine option defaults to false and returns an empty vec silently. (4) IDLE: exposed as its own coroutine with raw untagged events and an AtomicBool shutdown; timeout configurable in 0.6. iCloud caveats: omits the '* ENABLED' echo, has shipped malformed QRESYNC FETCH seq numbers, and io-imap silently skips undecodable untagged lines. Follow-ups filed as postio-wy2.1 through .4; postio-wy2.1 (live post-auth CAPABILITY assertion) is the one unverified assumption and is P1 before E4.2. No spike code written to the repo or workspace.

Added scripts/check-crate-boundaries.py: walks the resolved cargo metadata graph (normal+build deps transitively, plus the guarded crate's own dev-deps) and fails if postio-core reaches gtk4/libadwaita (or their -sys/gdk4/gsk4 companions) or postio-gtk reaches rusqlite/libsqlite3-sys/io-imap. Failure output names the offending crate, the offending dependency, the full path, and whether it is direct or transitive; a missing guarded crate is exit 2, not a silent pass. Package renames (postio-gtk uses gtk = {package = "gtk4"}) do not fool it. scripts/test-check-crate-boundaries.py builds throwaway path-only workspaces in a temp dir and proves the check fails for a direct gtk4 dep on postio-core, a transitive libadwaita dep, a direct rusqlite dep on postio-gtk, and an io-imap dev-dep - all 7 cases pass, no network, real manifests untouched. Both are wired into the CI 'Crate boundaries' job. Check is green on the current tree.

Added .github/workflows/ci.yml with four jobs: fmt (cargo fmt --all --check), boundaries (crate-boundary check + its self-test + a guard asserting no workflow opts into the ignored live-server tests), build (apt-installs libgtk-4-dev, libadwaita-1-dev, libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev, libsqlite3-dev, libsecret-1-dev, libglib2.0-dev, libpango1.0-dev, then clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test --workspace), and bench (detects bench targets via cargo metadata and skips cleanly while none exist, so the criterion harness bead can land with no workflow change). SyncState/MailboxStatus/ResyncPlan in postio-model::sync (pure, 10 unit tests) plus SyncStateRepository in postio-storage (14 integration tests). Never-synced is an explicit state (never_synced/has_synced), and plan() is one decision over the whole state so UIDVALIDITY outranks MODSEQ. Prerequisite fix: every repository opened its own BEGIN via unchecked_transaction, which SQLite refuses inside a caller's transaction — replaced with repository::Scope, a nesting-safe SAVEPOINT that rolls back on drop. That is what makes 'state updates and message writes commit in one transaction' actually reachable.

Operation vocabulary in postio-model::operation (Operation, OperationTarget, OperationState, OperationId) with 11 unit tests, and OperationQueueRepository in postio-storage with 15 integration tests. Every op type has a decided, tested inverse: set/clear flags swap, move swaps its ends, delete inverts to a move back out of the trash; expunge/append/send are irreversible on purpose and enqueue_inverse returns Error::NotUndoable rather than pretending. Undo is enqueue_inverse onto the same queue, so there is one drain path. Enqueue nests in the caller's transaction (repository::Scope) and keeps messages.has_pending_operations true; restart order verified against a reopened file-backed database. Vocabulary went in postio-model, not postio-sync, because postio-core's undo stack and the GTK undo toast both need it and neither can reach postio-sync.

postio_gtk::keymap: Chord/Binding parser, Keymap table, Resolver. 31 unit tests plus 4 integration tests, all display-free. gg vs G resolve as a sequence vs a single press; Esc resolves per context (list clear_selection / thread back / composer / search / palette) via KeyContext::chain, with Composer/Search/Palette deliberately NOT falling back through the list. Text entry wins: a chord fires while typing only if it carries ctrl/alt/super, or is Escape or a function key — shift alone does not count, so 'shift+a' is still the letter A. Shift is folded into the character for printable keys, which is what makes 'a' and 'A' separate bindings and what GDK actually delivers. Pending chords expire after CHORD_TIMEOUT (1s, injectable clock) and Outcome::Pending carries the display string for the visible pending indicator. Chord::from_key_event is the only GTK-facing surface. Keymap::shadowed() reports bindings a shorter one makes unreachable rather than refusing to start. Added a dev-dep on postio-config so a test pins the two binding parsers to the same syntax.

The defaults were already registry data (postio-core::registry); what was missing was that they could actually be pressed. Three things landed:

1. Fixed first_message: its default was "gg", which neither binding parser accepts — a chord sequence is whitespace-separated, so "gg" reads as a key named 'gg'. Now "g g", with a registry test asserting every built-in binding (primary and alternate) passes postio_config::keys::binding_problem. postio-config only validated user overrides, so the built-ins had no guard at all.

2. postio_gtk::keymap::Keymap::from_commands(&postio_core::Keymap) — the bridge from the registry to the resolver's table, plus From<Context> for KeyContext. A ContextSet::ANY command binds once in KeyContext::Global rather than six times, so a specific context can still claim the key. Unparseable bindings are returned as problems, never a panic.

3. docs/keybindings.md, rendered from the registry by crates/postio-core/tests/keybindings_doc.rs, which fails when the file drifts (POSTIO_UPDATE_DOCS=1 regenerates).

12 integration tests in crates/postio-gtk/tests/keymap_defaults.rs, all display-free, including one that walks every registry entry in every context it claims and asserts the binding reaches that command — that is the 'every canvas binding works' criterion.

NOT done: the README. There is no README.md in the repo yet and postio-b1z owns it (and is blocked by this bead precisely so it can cite the final set). b1z should link docs/keybindings.md rather than restate it. postio-sync now exists: coalesce.rs, retry.rs, drain.rs. 24 unit tests + 19 integration tests, all against MockBackend with no network.

COALESCING (16 unit tests): folds a batch per target, in order. Same-direction flag changes union; opposite directions cancel on the overlap; moves chain through their midpoint and cancel when they return to the origin; a move followed by a delete deletes from where the message actually started (otherwise the drainer selects a mailbox the message has left). Append/Send/Expunge never fold and act as barriers nothing folds across. Plan::rows() is asserted equal to the batch size in a test — a row that is neither planned nor obsolete would be a lost mutation.

RETRY (8 unit tests): exponential, base 2s, doubling, capped at 5min, 8 attempts. A server's Retry-After wins when longer and is ignored when shorter. Saturating arithmetic so an absurd attempt count lands on the ceiling instead of wrapping to a short wait. Deliberately no jitter — the queue drains serially within an account, so there is no herd here; that belongs to the connection loop (postio-c78).

CONFLICTS: the interesting finding is that IMAP does not report a vanished message. STORE against a UID that has left the mailbox succeeds and says nothing. So the drainer reads what came back: a store over a non-empty UID set that updated nothing means the message is gone -> Obsolete, settled not failed, and the mailbox goes into DrainReport::needs_resync. A move is checked the same way but ONLY under UIDPLUS, because without it an empty mapping is the ordinary answer and carries no information. Tested: deleted-remotely, moved-both-sides (asserts the message is not duplicated), UIDVALIDITY renumbered (failed rather than retried — retrying would act on whatever message now holds that UID), never-uploaded message, deleted destination mailbox.

FAILURES ARE LOUD: every row ends Applied, Obsolete, Deferred or Failed; nothing is dropped. A failed row keeps its reason and appears in DrainReport::failed, and a later pass does not silently retry it. A folded step defers or fails every row behind it together.

Also added: OperationQueueRepository::note (records why a row settled without a round trip, without changing its state) and crates/postio-sync/tests/boundary.rs.

On that boundary test — I first tried adding postio-sync to scripts/check-crate-boundaries.py and it cannot work: cargo unifies features across a workspace, so postio-imap builds with its default 'imap' feature on and io-imap is in the resolved graph no matter what this crate asks for. A graph check would fail a correct crate. What actually holds the line is that io-imap is not a dependency of postio-sync, so 'use io_imap::' does not compile. The test guards the manifest instead, which is the thing an edit could quietly change.

NOT in scope, and failed loudly rather than skipped: Operation::Send and Operation::Append need the SMTP transport and the blob store (postio-pzy, which this bead was blocking).

postio_gtk::palette plus the keyboard path in window.rs. 17 unit tests (no display) and one on-display widget test.

MATCHING is pure and display-free: score() is a greedy left-to-right subsequence match, case-insensitive, with a word-start bonus, a consecutive-run bonus and a capped gap penalty, returning the matched byte positions so rows can bold them. entries() filters by Context, ranks, and reads each binding from the live postio_core::Keymap. Commands are findable by stable id as well as title, with a penalty so a title match always outranks an id match for the same query.

WIDGET: a plate over the workspace in a gtk::Overlay, so the panes stay visible behind it. It rebuilds the whole list on every keystroke — thirty rows, microseconds, and it cannot leave a stale row behind the way an incremental update can. Down/Up/Enter/Escape are handled on the search entry at the capture phase so the cursor never leaves it.

Two things found by testing on the real display:
1. gtk::SearchEntry debounces search-changed by 150ms. Right for a search that hits a database, wrong for a palette the bead says must filter instantly — switched to the immediate 'changed' signal.
2. The palette's entry originally wore .postio-search, which broke gtk_shell.rs: that test measures the header's search field by finding the first widget with that class, and ToolbarView puts content before top bars. The palette now has .postio-palette-search and the stylesheet groups the two, so .postio-search still means the header's field.

KEYBOARD, in window.rs: the window now owns a keymap::Resolver and an EventControllerKey at the capture phase, and Window::handle_key is public so a test can press a key without synthesizing a GDK event (GTK4 offers no supported way). It acts only on the commands that are about the window — open the palette, close what is open — and hands everything else to connect_command. Window::apply_keymap rebuilds the resolver and the palette together. app.rs now lays the user's [keys] over the registry defaults on activate; the Window itself stays on defaults so the widget tests remain hermetic.

BUDGET: ten consecutive rebuilds and one open are asserted well inside the 16ms interaction budget. That is a smoke test against an accidental O(n*m); cargo bench (postio-v45) owns the real numbers.

postio_sync::connect: ReconnectPolicy, Link, Blocker, NetworkState, Supervisor. 9 unit tests for the schedule + 15 integration tests against MockBackend.

THE FLAPPING INSIGHT, which is what the bead is really about: resetting the attempt count the moment a connection succeeds sounds right and is the bug. A link that comes up and drops again every second never gets past the first backoff step, so the client reconnects as fast as the link can fail. So a success only clears the count once the connection has HELD for ReconnectPolicy::stability (30s default). The test runs ten connect-then-drop cycles and asserts the attempt count climbs 1..=10 rather than staying at 1, and that the tenth wait is 20x the first.

JITTER: unlike the operation queue (postio-s45), reconnection genuinely has a herd — every account, and on a shared server every client, returns at the same instant after an outage. Equal jitter: half the backoff plus a random share of the other half. Full jitter was rejected because it can return almost zero, which puts a client that was just refused straight back on the server's door. The entropy is an ARGUMENT, not something the module reaches for, which is what makes the schedule unit-testable: a test asserts every delay lands in [backoff/2, backoff] across attempts 1..12 and eight entropy values, and that 64 different seeds produce >32 distinct delays.

NEVER SPIN: an auth failure goes to Link::Blocked(Authentication) and the test then polls 29 more times over half an hour and asserts backend.calls() did not move. retry_now() is what "the user typed a new password" means. Anything else non-transient becomes Blocked(Unrecoverable) — deliberately not broken down further, because BackendError is #[non_exhaustive] and asks callers to branch on its predicates rather than its variants.

Link::Offline is a separate state from Link::Waiting on purpose: with no network there is nothing to retry against, so attempts are not spent and the status line says "offline" rather than counting down to a reconnection that cannot succeed. Bringing the network back sets retry_at to now, so a laptop lid opening reconnects immediately instead of waiting out a backoff measured against a network that no longer exists. A wrong password stays wrong across a network change.

Also honours BackendError::retry_after when the server asks for longer than our own backoff.

NOT DONE, filed as postio-0d9.1: the actual NetworkManager D-Bus listener. set_network is the seam and everything above it is built and tested; the listener needs a main loop and a system bus, and putting either in postio-sync would cost the property that the whole engine tests with no bus. On a machine with no NetworkManager the default NetworkState::Unknown already behaves correctly — refusing to try because NM could not be found would be worse than trying and failing, and there is a test for that.

Also worth noting for whoever wires the engine loop: Supervisor::observe(&BackendError, now) is how the drainer and fetchers report a mid-command drop, and Drainer::drain already returns SyncError::Backend for a pass that died at the top. Nothing connects the two yet — that is the engine loop, which does not exist.

postio_gtk::cheatsheet: 9 unit tests (no display) plus tests/gtk_cheatsheet.rs on the real display.

GENERATED: sections(&postio_core::Keymap) is a pure function over the registry, so 'rebinding a key changes the cheat sheet with no code edit' is a two-line test — override archive to y, call Window::apply_keymap, read the row back. Window::apply_keymap now reprints the resolver, the palette and the sheet together.

GROUPING was the design decision worth making. Most registry commands are reachable in three or four contexts, so the naive rendering lists 'Archive' under Message list, Thread AND Reading. A reader scanning for 'how do I archive' wants one answer. So a command reachable everywhere (ContextSet::ANY) goes under 'Everywhere', which leads; everything else goes under the first — and therefore broadest — context it applies in. A test asserts every registry command appears exactly once and that the totals match. ACCESSIBILITY: the sheet is AccessibleRole::Dialog with a label, because that is what it behaves like. Test-file note for whoever adds more GTK tests: the cheat sheet test is its own file rather than a second function in gtk_palette.rs. The last hop landed: postio_gtk::config bridges the watcher's thread to the main context, so an edit to config.toml now rebinds a running window.

WHY IT WAS STUCK: postio-config reparses and validates on its own thread (so a broken file never costs the UI a frame) and hands back a Checked, which is Send. Every GTK widget is main-thread only and not Send, so the watcher's callback cannot touch the window. The bridge is an async_channel whose Sender goes to the watcher thread and whose Receiver is awaited by a glib::spawn_future_local task on the main context, where the window is. The watcher is moved into that task so it lives exactly as long as the reader.

postio_model::threading (20 unit tests) + postio_storage::repository::threading (19 integration tests, corpus-driven) + migration 0002_thread_links.

THE DESIGN DECISION: JWZ is written as a batch pass — build a container table, link, prune, group by subject. That is the right shape for a mailbox you have just been handed and the wrong shape for Postio, where messages arrive one at a time forever. So the linkage RULE is kept and the PASS is discarded. threading::assign answers one question — which thread does this message belong to — by asking a ThreadIndex about the ids the message names. Pure, so the rule is tested exhaustively in postio-model and the storage layer is tested separately for whether its lookups are cheap.

WHAT MAKES IT O(thread): a new table, thread_links, holding every Message-ID a thread has ever mentioned, present or absent, primary-keyed on (account_id, rfc_message_id). The messages table cannot answer the question: rfc_message_id is indexed but reference_ids is a space-separated list, so finding a thread that REFERENCES an id would scan the mailbox. Proof is a test that files one message into a 30-message mailbox and into a 600-message one and asserts the statement count is IDENTICAL, plus one that a 40-deep reference chain stays linear.

OUT-OF-ORDER AND MERGING FALL OUT TOGETHER: a thread claims ids it has never seen, so a reply arriving before its parent claims the parent's id and the parent joins the thread waiting for it. When a message names ids held by two threads, assign returns Merge and the caller folds one into the other — no separate detection pass and no way for the two to disagree. Oldest thread survives, absorb list sorted, both deterministic.

BUG FOUND WHILE TESTING: the first version merged then relinked. ThreadRepository::merge deletes the absorbed thread and thread_links.thread_id cascades on that delete, so every id the absorbed thread had claimed was silently dropped and the conversation came apart on the next reply. Relink now happens before the merge, with a comment saying why.

CORPUS: the list-thread-01..07 fixtures thread as one conversation, including the one with In-Reply-To but no References and the one with neither. broken-references.eml, duplicate-message-id.eml and every other fixture in the corpus are filed without panicking or being left unthreaded.

KNOWN LIMITATION, filed as postio-tn9.2 and asserted rather than hidden: arriving newest-first, list-thread-06-reply-subject-only is stranded. It carries no In-Reply-To and no References, so its subject is the only thing that could place it, and it arrives before the messages sharing that subject — the only thread that exists at that moment was started by list-thread-07-subject-change, whose subject is deliberately different. Nothing available at that instant places it correctly, and re-deriving it later means rethreading the mailbox, which is the cost this design exists to avoid. Every message that carries a usable reference converges from either direction.

Subject fallback keeps JWZ's safeguard: it applies only when there is no reference link at all AND the subject carries reply decoration (new postio_model::subject::is_reply), so two people saying 'Hello' are not a conversation. A bracketed list tag is kept, so two lists are two conversations.

postio_gtk::search: 19 unit tests (no display) plus tests/gtk_search.rs on the real display.

WHY THE ENTRY HOLDS THE WHOLE QUERY: the tempting design lifts completed operators out of the entry into standalone chips. It is a nicer picture and a worse editor — the caret can no longer move through the query and every edit becomes a merge between two representations. Here the entry is the truth and the chips are a parse of it drawn alongside. That is also plainly what postio-search's API was designed for: ParsedQuery hands out Spans INTO the input, token_at documents that both edges count 'so a caret resting against either end of a chip still selects it', and remove_token is documented as returning what the search bar sets its entry to.

BACKSPACE: pops when the caret is inside a chip or against its RIGHT edge — which is where it sits after typing one. Against the left edge the caret is before the chip, so Backspace deletes the space as usual; otherwise there is no way to remove the space in front of a chip. Free text is never popped whole: subject:report is one idea, but a word the user typed is a word.

CARET UNITS: GTK counts the cursor in characters and the parser's spans are in bytes. They differ the moment somebody searches for a name with an accent in it, so SearchBar::caret converts.

ESC RESTORES: the window records (Context, Pane) before anything moves and puts both back on close, so the keyboard returns where the user left it. Reopening starts empty — a bar that reopens showing the last search has to be cleared first. Selection restoration is the list's and lands with postio-5dz/agr; the pane and context halves are done and tested.

TYPING WINS: entering the bar puts focus in a GtkText, so the resolver's text-entry rule suppresses single-key bindings — the test presses  in the bar and asserts nothing archived.

ROOT-CAUSE FIX WORTH KNOWING: this is the second widget to trip gtk_shell.rs, which asserts the header's search field is 600px by finding the first widget in the WINDOW with .postio-search — and AdwToolbarView puts content before top bars. I dodged it for the palette by giving it a private class; that left the trap armed. The locator is now scoped to the header bar's own subtree, which is what the assertion always meant, and the palette's duplicate class and its CSS grouping are gone again. Every search-shaped field wears .postio-search and they read as one control.

Chips are IBM Plex Mono because they are syntax, with distinct treatments for partial (dashed, no fill) and negated (outlined) so -from:someone does not look like from:someone. Each carries an accessible label reading 'from ada@example.com' or 'not is unread' rather than the shorthand.
